Clinicians treat injuries, offer emergency contraception and pregnancy testing, assess and offer STI prophylaxis (per CDC 2021: ceftriaxone, doxycycline and metronidazole), hepatitis B vaccination if not immune, HPV vaccination as appropriate, and HIV postexposure prophylaxis started within 72 hours when risk justifies. Mental health support and safety planning are key, and mandatory reporting rules differ by state for minors and for some adults. Medicolegal documentation records the patient's own words.

Intimate partner violence is common, and the USPSTF (2018, reaffirmed June 2025) recommends screening women of reproductive age, including those who are pregnant or postpartum, and providing or referring those who screen positive to support services. Pregnancy can be a period of increased risk. Screening is done privately, with safety assessment, documentation, and a referral to advocacy and shelter services, while clinicians avoid pressuring the patient to leave and respect her autonomy and risk assessment. Clinicians must know reporting laws, which vary.

A worked example: a 23-year-old arrives 36 hours after an assault. After consent, the team offers evidence collection (which she may decline or defer), emergency contraception, STI prophylaxis, hepatitis B and HIV prophylaxis evaluation, and referrals, while letting her decide on police involvement.

questions.prompt: Which change in renal physiology is expected in normal pregnancy?
choices: Decreased glomerular filtration rate with a higher serum creatinine
Unchanged filtration with increased tubular reabsorption of glucose
Increased filtration with a higher serum creatinine from dilution
Increased glomerular filtration rate with a lower serum creatinine

questions.prompt: A 29-year-old at 27 weeks is Rh-negative with a negative antibody screen and an Rh-positive partner. Which management is correct?
choices: Repeat antibody screens monthly with intrauterine transfusion planned from 32 weeks
Immune globulin only if the woman develops bleeding during the pregnancy
Anti-D immune globulin at 28 weeks and after delivery
No treatment until delivery, when cord blood determines whether immune globulin is needed

questions.prompt: A 32-year-old woman at 10 weeks has chronic hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Which intervention reduces her risk of preeclampsia?
choices: Prophylactic labetalol started once blood pressure exceeds 120/80
Low-dose aspirin started before 16 weeks
Calcium and vitamin D supplements taken in the first trimester
Bed rest at home from the beginning of the second trimester

questions.prompt: A pregnant woman at 30 weeks has not received Tdap. Which statement is most accurate?
choices: Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks in every pregnancy
Tdap is contraindicated in pregnancy and should be given immediately after delivery
Tdap is given only in the first pregnancy because the antibody persists for life
Tdap is given only if the household contains an unvaccinated adult

questions.prompt: A woman with hypertension has just discovered she is 7 weeks pregnant while taking lisinopril. Which fetal effect is the greatest concern if exposure continues into the second and third trimesters?
choices: Neural tube defects with anencephaly
Ebstein anomaly with tricuspid regurgitation
Phocomelia with limb shortening
Renal dysgenesis with oligohydramnios

questions.prompt: Which statement describes cell-free DNA screening?
choices: A sensitive screen whose positives need confirmation
It is a diagnostic test equivalent to amniocentesis and can be used alone
It is only available to women older than 35 who have an abnormal ultrasound
It detects neural tube defects with high sensitivity from maternal blood

questions.prompt: A quadruple screen at 17 weeks shows low AFP, low oestriol, high hCG and high inhibin A. Which condition does this pattern suggest?
choices: Turner syndrome with cystic hygroma
Down syndrome
Edwards syndrome
Open neural tube defect

questions.prompt: A 25-year-old at 12 weeks receives a positive cell-free DNA screen for trisomy 18, with no ultrasound abnormalities. Which statement best describes the next step?
choices: Repeat the same screen in four weeks and act only if it remains positive
Reassure the patient that a normal ultrasound excludes the diagnosis
Genetic counselling and diagnostic CVS or amniocentesis
Recommend immediate termination, since the screen has more than 99 percent specificity

questions.prompt: An Rh-negative woman at 20 weeks has a positive indirect Coombs test with high titre anti-D. What is the best method for assessing fetal anaemia?
choices: Administration of anti-D immune globulin to halt the sensitisation
Serial maternal haemoglobin measurement to follow fetal haemoglobin
Biophysical profile each week
Middle cerebral artery Doppler velocimetry

questions.prompt: A pregnant woman at 18 weeks has an elevated maternal serum AFP. Ultrasound shows normal anatomy and a gestational age by crown-rump length 3 weeks less than by menstrual dates. What is the most likely explanation?
choices: Dating error from inaccurate menstrual dates
A fetal open neural tube defect missed by ultrasound
Fetal abdominal wall defect with normal ultrasound findings
Placental mosaicism for trisomy 18

questions.prompt: According to ACOG and SMFM (2014), at what cervical dilation does the active phase of labour generally begin?
choices: 8 cm
6 cm
3 cm
4 cm

questions.prompt: A fetal heart tracing shows decelerations that begin after the peak of each contraction and return to baseline after it ends, with moderate variability. What is the most likely mechanism?
choices: Uteroplacental insufficiency
Fetal head compression
Umbilical cord compression
Fetal sleep cycle

questions.prompt: A woman at 8 cm dilation has a tracing with absent variability and recurrent late decelerations. Intrauterine resuscitation measures are tried for 20 minutes without change. What is the most appropriate next step?
choices: Continue oxytocin to complete labour and delivery
Fetal scalp stimulation and repeat monitoring in an hour
Amnioinfusion to correct the late decelerations
Expedited delivery, by cesarean if not imminent

questions.prompt: Which fetal heart rate feature best reflects an intact, well-oxygenated fetal central nervous system?
choices: Early decelerations
Absence of any accelerations
Moderate baseline variability
A baseline rate of 160 beats per minute

choices: Membrane stripping alone, repeated each day
Cervical ripening with prostaglandin or a balloon
Intravenous oxytocin started without any cervical preparation
Immediate cesarean delivery, because the cervix is unfavourable

choices: Strong downward traction on the fetal head
Immediate Zavanelli manoeuvre followed by cesarean delivery
The McRoberts manoeuvre with suprapubic pressure
Fundal pressure to push the shoulder under the symphysis

choices: Normal latent phase, so continue waiting for several more hours
Failed induction, so restart the oxytocin infusion at a higher rate
Second-stage arrest, so apply forceps for delivery
Active-phase arrest, for which cesarean delivery is indicated

TOLAC is contraindicated because any prior cesarean carries a high rupture risk
She may labour only if she accepts prostaglandin ripening to speed delivery
TOLAC is appropriate only at a home birth where intervention is minimal

choices: It is recommended in all women with a transverse lie once labour has begun
It succeeds in about half of attempts and is contraindicated in placenta previa
It is performed only after the onset of labour with ruptured membranes

choices: Induction should be refused because it raises perinatal mortality
Induction is appropriate only after 41 weeks for any indication

Induction at 39 weeks doubled the cesarean rate compared with expectant care

questions.prompt: Which drug is given to women at risk of delivery before 32 weeks to reduce the risk of cerebral palsy in the infant?
choices: Terbutaline
Indomethacin
Methyldopa
Magnesium sulfate

choices: Digital cervical examination to assess dilation
Outpatient observation with weekly visits until 37 weeks
Admit, give steroids and latency antibiotics, deliver near 34 weeks
Immediate induction of labour with oxytocin

choices: Cesarean delivery for all cases of intraamniotic infection
Broad antibiotics and delivery, cesarean only if indicated
Indomethacin tocolysis and expectant management for steroid administration
Antibiotics alone with delivery delayed until 34 weeks

choices: To delay delivery about 48 hours for steroids
To prevent preterm birth until term
To provide fetal neuroprotection
To mature the fetal lungs

choices: Bed rest at home until 34 weeks
Prophylactic tocolysis with nifedipine from 20 weeks
Antenatal betamethasone started at 20 weeks
Ultrasound-indicated cervical cerclage placement

choices: Uterine atony
Retained placental tissue
Genital tract lacerations
Coagulopathy

choices: Amniotomy to check for meconium
Ultrasound to locate the placenta first
Digital cervical examination to assess dilation
Immediate induction with oxytocin

Amniotic band syndrome
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Cord prolapse from rupture of membranes

choices: Misoprostol
Carboprost in a woman without asthma
Tranexamic acid
Methylergonovine

choices: Planned preterm cesarean hysterectomy at a specialist centre
Vaginal delivery after induction, with manual removal of the placenta
Cesarean delivery at 39 weeks, with manual placental removal as usual
Expectant management until spontaneous labour at term

choices: Levetiracetam
Magnesium sulfate
Phenytoin
Diazepam

choices: Stop the magnesium and give intravenous calcium gluconate
Increase the infusion rate to control further seizures
Administer naloxone for opioid-induced respiratory depression
Give a bolus of normal saline and continue the infusion

Plasma exchange for presumed thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
Intravenous ursodeoxycholic acid with induction at 37 weeks
Magnesium sulfate and delivery after maternal stabilisation

choices: Nifedipine
Methyldopa
Lisinopril
Labetalol

choices: Start oral methyldopa and discharge without any further testing
Delivery at 37 weeks, since she has preeclampsia without severe features
Immediate cesarean delivery for suspected eclampsia
Continue expectant management until 41 weeks for a vaginal birth

choices: Neonatal thyrotoxicosis
Limb reduction defects
Caudal regression syndrome
Fetal alcohol spectrum

choices: Bed rest and calorie restriction
Immediate delivery at 37 weeks
Oral sulfonylurea as first-line agent
Insulin therapy

Continue all medications through pregnancy, since stopping them risks worse control

Delay folic acid until the first prenatal visit

Await spontaneous labour up to 40 weeks 6 days
Deliver by cesarean at 37 weeks

HbA1c at 1 week postpartum, which is the preferred test at that time
75 g oral glucose tolerance test at 4 to 12 weeks, then lifelong periodic screening

A normal-sized uterus and low hCG

Misoprostol for presumed incomplete miscarriage
Methotrexate, after baseline laboratory tests

hCG stimulating the TSH receptor via a shared alpha subunit

Threatened abortion
Missed abortion

Cholecystectomy during pregnancy

Endometritis
Atelectasis
Mastitis

Sertraline monotherapy with review in four weeks

Withhold information about the option to avoid giving moral approval to it

The Court held that mifepristone approval violated federal law and removed the drug
